# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, list $299)**
- Runner's World ranks them #1 for comfort, sound, and stability. WIRED praises the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and they can be quiet in heavy traffic.
- Runner's World says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- Buy options: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) (Bose, Amazon, Walmart links) or [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (list $180, listed around $125 at Best Buy and REI)**
- Rated IP55 with 12 hours of battery and physical controls. WIRED calls it the best option if you want more bass while staying aware of your surroundings.
- Downsides: the neckband can clash with long hair or hoods, and clarity is a bit below Bose.
- [WIRED review with retailer links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long, wet runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- WIRED's top pick overall. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating.
- [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 at Amazon)**
- SoundGuys' best overall and best for running. It has strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a good EQ app.
- [SoundGuys' guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best ear-hook budget pick: Soundcore AeroFit 2**
- IP55, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), and a hook that stays put.
- SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon: [SoundGuys' guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/).
- A Dealectric page lists it at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20, at [Soundcore's store](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). That's an affiliate link, and Dealectric says it tested the code on 2026-10-22. Since that price is well above Amazon's, compare before buying.

**Cheapest way to try the category: JLab Flex Open (~$40) or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (~$50)**
- Runner's World liked the JLab for the price, though it has less bass and detail. WIRED recommends the PearlClip Pro as a low-risk first pair.
- [JLab at Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [PearlClip Pro at WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guidance**
- Want the most awareness, or wear glasses and hats? Choose Shokz bone conduction.
- Want the best sound? Choose Bose.
- Want the most durable? Choose OpenDots 2.
- On a budget? Choose the Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're a poor fit for loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Prices shift often, so confirm at checkout.
